knowledge:
- key_parameters: filterPerc=Minimum percentage of samples with an expression value of 0 to remove genes during RNA-seq filtering (default is 0.75) ;; database=The pathway database to use, such as "KEGG", "reactome", or a file path to a custom MSigDB GMT file ;; analysis=The type of expression data being analyzed, either "microarray" or "RNAseq" ;; databaseGeneFormat=The gene identifier format used in the custom database (e.g., "ENTREZID") ;; expressionSetGeneFormat=The gene identifier format used in the ExpressionSet (e.g., "PROBEID", "ENSEMBL", "SYMBOL") ;; limma.cutoff=The significance threshold for the LIMMA model to filter out flat genes (default is 0.05) ;; cor.cutoff=The correlation threshold used to identify highly correlated partner genes (default is 0.85)
- alternatives: Custom MSigDB gene sets (provided via a GMT file) can be used as an alternative to the default KEGG or Reactome pathway databases.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing transcriptomics data (microarray or RNA-seq) across multiple distinct cell types, stem cell lines, or experimental groups to identify core driving pathways, co-expressed gene modules, and their functional roles.
- pitfalls: When using RNA-seq datasets, the expressionSetGeneFormat argument in findAttractors must always be explicitly declared (e.g., "ENSEMBL", "ENTREZID", or "SYMBOL") ;; The cellTypeTag argument must exactly match one of the column names in the phenoData of the ExpressionSet (colnames(pData(eSet))).

workflows.name: microarray_attractor_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify core attractor pathways, synexpression groups, correlated partner genes, and functional enrichment from microarray gene expression data.
input: samp.info (data frame of sample and cell type annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load data and construct ExpressionSet ;; 2. Find core attractor pathway modules ;; 3. Filter out flat or uninformative genes ;; 4. Find synexpression groups for a pathway or top pathways ;; 5. Plot synexpression group profiles ;; 6. Find correlated partner genes across the genome ;; 7. Calculate functional enrichment of synexpression groups
workflows.code:
library(attract)
data(exprs.dat) 
data(samp.info)
loring.eset <- new("ExpressionSet")
loring.eset@assayData <- new.env()
assign("exprs", exprs.dat, loring.eset@assayData)
p.eset <- new("AnnotatedDataFrame", data=samp.info)
loring.eset@phenoData <- p.eset
attractor.states <- findAttractors(loring.eset, "celltype", 
                                   annotation="illuminaHumanv1.db", 
                                   database="KEGG",analysis="microarray",
                                   databaseGeneFormat=NULL, expressionSetGeneFormat=NULL)
remove.these.genes <- removeFlatGenes(loring.eset, "celltype", 
                                      contrasts=NULL, limma.cutoff=0.05)
mapk.syn <- findSynexprs("04010", attractor.states, "celltype"
                         , remove.these.genes)
top5.syn <- findSynexprs(attractor.states@rankedPathways[1:5,1], 
                         attractor.states, "celltype", 
                         removeGenes=remove.these.genes)
par(mfrow=c(2,2)) 
pretty.col <- rainbow(3) 
for( i in 1:3 ){
	plotsynexprs(mapk.syn, tickMarks=c(6, 28, 47, 60), 
               tickLabels=c("ESC", "PRO", "NSC", "TER"), 
               vertLines=c(12.5, 43.5, 51.5), index=i, 
			main=paste("Synexpression Group ", i, sep="")
      ,col=pretty.col[i])
 }
mapk.cor <- findCorrPartners(mapk.syn, loring.eset, remove.these.genes)
mapk.func <- calcFuncSynexprs(mapk.syn, attractor.states, "CC", 
                              annotation="illuminaHumanv1.db"
                              ,analysis="microarray",expressionSetGeneFormat=NULL)

workflows.name: rnaseq_custom_gmt_attractor_analysis
workflows.intent: Filter RNA-seq expression data and identify core attractor pathways using a custom MSigDB GMT file with explicit gene format mapping.
input: data (data frame of RNA-seq expression data)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter RNA-seq data to remove low-expression genes ;; 2. Find core attractor pathway modules using a custom GMT database and explicit gene format specifications
workflows.code:
library(attract)
filteredData <- filterDataSet(data, filterPerc=0.75)
MSigDBpath <- system.file("extdata","c4.cgn.v5.0.entrez.gmt",package="attract")
attractor.states.cutsom <- findAttractors(loring.eset, "celltype", annotation="illuminaHumanv1.db",database=MSigDBpath, analysis="microarray",databaseGeneFormat="ENTREZID", expressionSetGeneFormat="PROBEID")
